title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Penumbra Insurance
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Penumbra through the SIG questionnaire items most relevant to PII/regulated data: SOC 2 scope, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and data residency. Penumbra asked for evidence artifacts and timelines for SOC2 report, encryption architecture diagram, and details on private deployment options. Next steps agreed: share SOC2 Type II, CAIQ answers, architecture diagram, and schedule a follow-up technical deep dive and pilot benchmark window.
next_steps: James Carter - Share SOC 2 Type II report and CAIQ answers by 2026-09-17
Priya Nair - Provide KMS/encryption architecture diagram and RBAC/SSO configuration notes by 2026-09-18
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with Marcus and Priya for 2026-09-24
Elena Ruiz - confirm procurement timeline and required contract terms by 2026-09-21
action_items: James: upload SOC2 report link to CRM and email Penumbra
Priya: prepare short runbook for evidence requests (audit logs, retention)
Liam: prepare list of potential dedicated/private deployment SKUs and costs
Tom: circulate internal threat model questions ahead of next call
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 56 minutes | Attendees: James Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (RD), Tom Watson (CISO - Penumbra), Marcus Lee (Sec Eng), Elena Ruiz (Procurement), Ava Chen (Legal)

[00:00] James: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Tom: yes loud and clear, thanks James. we wanted to go through the SIG and CAIQ, mostly around SOC2 scope and encryption stuff.
[00:10] James: great, our plan is Priya will run through the security controls mapping, i'll handle contract and compliance artifacts and liam will chime in on deployment options. sound good?
[00:17] Elena: yes that's perfect. we have a short list of must-haves: SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML with SCIM, audit logs with retention options, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[00:28] Priya: ok on SOC2 we are currently SOC 2 Type II for the inference and control plane, report scope includes change mgmt, access controls, availability, and confidentiality; small note the report references our hosted api and dedicated offerings but private on-prem has separate attestation conversations.
[00:43] Marcus: when you say dedicated offering, does that mean data is co-mingled or isolated? we need guaranteed tenant isolation and encryption at rest with our key.
[00:51] Priya: dedicated is isolated tenant pools, data at rest is encrypted; for customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS providers via BYOK/HSM workflows, we can provide architecture diagram.
[01:01] Tom: curious about key rotation, and whether Redwood can access plaintext for support or debugging.
[01:06] James: good q. short answer: with customer-managed keys we do not have decryption rights, keys are under customer control in supported KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). support workflows may request logs or redacted data but we do not keep master keys.
[01:19] Ava: any legal exceptions or emergency access clauses? we will need to see the contract language.
[01:23] James: we'll surface the standard contract clause and note any enterprise addendum options, we'll include that in the next email.
[01:28] [00:30] Priya: on SSO/RBAC we support SAML 2.0 with SCIM user provisioning, role-based access controls map to org/route/model level, you can restrict actions like model rollout and key management to admins.
[01:40] Marcus: how granular are the roles? can we integrate with our existing IdP and map groups to roles?
[01:45] Priya: yes, group-to-role mappings and custom roles are supported; there is an admin and operator and viewer out of the box, we can add custom roles for e.g. "model-pusher".
[01:52] Elena: audit logs - what events are captured and how long are they retained?
[01:56] Priya: audit logs capture auth events, API calls, model deploys, config changes, and billing events; retention defaults to 90 days in hosted, enterprise/privates can extend retention and ship logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[02:10] Marcus: format and tamper-proofing? we need immutable logs for compliance.
[02:14] Priya: logs are append-only in our system and we can provide signed/exported logs for the retention window; for private deployments you can forward to your own immutable log store.
[02:22] [00:60] James: on data residency, we have region controls; hosted region options in US, EU, APAC partners; dedicated pools can be pinned to region, private on-prem obviously stays in your network. do you have a residency requirement?
[02:36] Tom: yes EU customer data must remain in eu-west, and some records must remain in-country. we also have re-identification risk concerns around embeddings.
[02:45] Priya: ok on embeddings we support token-level redaction at prefix cache and recommend client-side pseudonymization for higher-risk PII; we also have reranking and in-house token filtering. will include our guidance doc.
[02:56] Elena: for the SIG CAIQ there are some evidence items like architecture diagrams, encryption key mgmt screenshots, and the SOC2 report. can you confirm you can provide those?
[03:04] James: yes we can provide SOC2 Type II redacted pdf, CAIQ answered matrix, architecture diagram for KMS integration, and sample audit log export. for some items we may provide redacted screenshots rather than live consoles.
[03:14] Marcus: timeline? we need artifacts within a week ideally.
[03:17] James: we will try for 48-72 hours for the majority, SOC2 report we can share today if redacted, otherwise by EOD tomorrow.
[03:23] Ava: are there any outstanding third-party vendor risks? you mentioned some model partner infra?
[03:27] Priya: we use curated open models and a few upstream model weights from community sources; we do vendor risk assessments and can provide a list of outsourced dependencies - compute cloud providers, monitoring, and a lightweight list of model sources.
[03:39] Tom: ok, procurement will need to see indemnities and data processing addendum (DPA).
[03:43] James: noted, we'll include DPA template and standard DPIA language.
[03:47] [00:45] Elena: about private deployment - what's the difference between Dedicated and Private?
[03:51] Liam: dedicated is Redwood-managed infrastructure reserved to you in our cloud regions; private is either a VPC peering or on-prem package where the control plane can be customer-managed and you can enforce network policies, complete air-gap option available for on-prem.
[04:03] Marcus: for dedicated, do you have hardware isolation options? single-tenant GPU hosts?
[04:07] Liam: yes dedicated can be single-tenant pools, we have options for pinned GPU racks; will share SKU and SLA matrix.
[04:13] Tom: performance/testing - can you support a small benchmark with our payloads?
[04:18] Priya: yes we'll set up a 2-week pilot window on a dedicated pool, priors: we'll need sample prompts, target latencies and QPS.
[04:25] James: next steps recap: we'll send SOC2, CAIQ, KMS diagram, DPA template, and proposed pilot dates; priya to run tech deep dive for pilot.
[04:33] Marcus: one more - incident response and notification SLAs.
[04:36] Priya: we have incident response playbooks, 24x7 on-call for P1 with notify within 1 hour for severe incidents, full post-mortem within 72 hours for P1. we'll include IR summary doc.
[04:47] Ava: contractually will you commit to certain notification windows?
[04:49] James: standard SLA language but enterprise addendum negotiable.
[04:53] [00:56] Tom: thanks, this was helpful. we'll look for the artifacts and set the follow-up.
[04:57] James: great, thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links after call.
[04:59] Elena: thanks all bye.
